solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Preferred feminine greeting, historically

parts.note: ave is the Latin word of greeting, hail, used in Roman times

explanation.surface: A note on the polite salutation once favoured when addressing a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite thing is the preferred one; the shortened informal form means the same.

clue.text: Where you could find ratings for energy pack?

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
a deck is a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: Seemingly a question about where to look up energy-efficiency labels on a battery pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ratings' suggests energy ratings but means ordinary sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratings are non-commissioned sailors, and the forward deck of a ship is where they could be found at work.

clue.text: Malevolent rodent almost beneath cooker, moving over

indicators.note: beneath places the shortened rodent under the cooker in this down answer
moving over says a letter of the word for cooker shifts from the front to the back

parts.note: an oven is a cooker

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the rodent is dropped

parts.note: a mouse is a small rodent

explanation.surface: A spiteful mouse that nearly scuttled out from under the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving over' turns OVEN into VENO; 'almost' cuts MOUSE to MOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Venomous means full of spite and malice, so it is a synonym of malevolent.

clue.text: Further book penned by singer's a little cleaner

parts.note: too means also, in addition, further

indicators.note: penned by means held inside, as in an enclosure, so the book goes inside the bird

parts.note: the thrush is a songbird, a singer

explanation.surface: A further volume written by a pop star turns out to be a bit of a whitewash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' suggests a vocalist, but it is a songbird; 'a little cleaner' looks like 'slightly cleaner' but means a small cleaning tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brush for scrubbing teeth is a little implement that cleans, so it is literally a little cleaner.

clue.text: Ancient line in poem forgotten, finally

indicators.note: in places the letter for line inside the word for poem

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An old verse in a poem that nobody remembers any more.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an old-fashioned word meaning of former times, ancient.

clue.text: Agent and therapist's top person entangling

indicators.note: top picks the first letter of the word, as in the top of a down entry

parts.note: someone who ravels things, tangles them up

explanation.surface: A spy and a senior psychotherapist caught up in a messy affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial traveller is a sales agent who travels to take orders for a firm.

clue.text: Trading phenomenon, the green equivalent of company car?

definitions.meaning: the regular rise and fall of economic activity, boom and bust

definitions.text: the green equivalent of company car?
definitions.meaning: an eco-friendly bike provided by one's employer, as a company car is

explanation.surface: An economic pattern, and the environmentally friendly perk replacing the firm's car.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the periodic swing of the economy and, punningly, a bicycle for work use.

clue.text: Apparently rational European ruined

parts.note: un-mad, not mad, is jokingly sane, apparently rational

explanation.surface: A seemingly sensible continental is brought to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unmade is undone, wrecked, ruined, as in 'made or unmade'.

clue.text: Fly goes through inverted trap

parts.note: to have something is to experience it, go through it, as in 'has a hard time'

indicators.note: inverted in a down answer says the word for trap is turned upside down

parts.note: a net is a trap for catching fish or birds

explanation.surface: An insect crawls into an upturned snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the insect but is the verb, to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly is to rush or speed, which is to hurry, the same as this verb.

clue.text: Engineers reversing charge briefly called again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: reversing tells us to read the shortened word for charge from back to front
briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the word for charge goes

parts.note: to demand a sum is to charge it

explanation.surface: Engineers backing down on a fee are given a fresh name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like an electrical or legal term but is a verb meaning to ask payment; 'Engineers' is a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given a new name has been named a second time, called again.

clue.text: Minor riot lad stirred, snaring unknown reptile

indicators.note: snaring means catching, so the unknown letter is caught inside the rearranged letters
stirred suggests mixing up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A youngster in a small disturbance gets caught up with a strange creature.
explanation.definitionFit: This large lizard of Africa, Asia and Australia is a reptile.

clue.text: Takes over when Aussie runner gets back on board

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: gets here means is taken in, so the reversed bird goes within the ship letters

parts.note: on board a ship, SS being the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: back says the word for the bird is read backwards

parts.note: the emu is a flightless Australian bird that runs

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge once an Australian athlete climbs back aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aussie runner' suggests an athlete but is the flightless bird; SS (steamship) is the crossword shorthand for being on board.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a role or responsibility is to take it on, to take over that duty.

clue.text: Authority and income tumbling

indicators.note: tumbling suggests the letters falling into disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Power and earnings both in freefall.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance is control or power over others, which is authority.

clue.text: Going in starkers is grand way to get attention

indicators.note: going in says the letter for grand is put inside the word for starkers

parts.note: starkers is British slang for naked, nude
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Streaking is a sure-fire way to make people notice you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starkers' is British slang for stark naked.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle poke with the elbow is a way of attracting someone's attention.

clue.text: Retort token bachelor has to endure

parts.note: a counter is a token used in games
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
to last is to endure, to go on

explanation.surface: A single man has to put up with a sharp comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigorous reply to an attack or argument is a retort.

clue.text: Shopmen trying to repeat dockers' work?

definitions.meaning: shopkeepers, those who sell goods to the public
people re-tailing, docking tails again, since one who docks a tail cuts it short

explanation.surface: Shop staff apparently attempting to redo the work of harbour labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dockers' suggests port workers, but here they dock tails.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopkeepers sell goods at retail, so they are the people who sell to the public.

clue.text: Drool when rising tardily about four

indicators.note: rising in a down answer means the word for when is read upwards

parts.note: as can mean when

indicators.note: about means around, so the late word goes round the numeral

parts.note: late means tardily, behind time
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone dribbling when they get up late, around four o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To salivate is to produce saliva, which is to drool.

clue.text: Lone woman threatening to seize power once one's gone

indicators.note: to seize means to grab hold of, so the shortened word holds the power letter
gone says the letter for one is removed

parts.note: sinister means threatening, menacing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single woman threatening to grab control after someone has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' removes I from SINISTER, leaving SINSTER, which takes in P.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinster is an unmarried woman, so traditionally a woman on her own.

clue.text: Fashion mart's price war, not a problem for correspondent

indicators.note: to fashion is to make or shape, so these letters are reworked into a new order
not says the letter a is left out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: A shop's discounting battle is no trouble for a journalist abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of MART'S PRICE WAR with one A taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cramp in the hand from long handwriting troubles someone who writes many letters.

clue.text: Settle raconteur's punch line?

definitions.meaning: the climax or final twist of a story

explanation.surface: A storyteller's closing gag that settles the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay off a debt is to settle it, and the payoff of a story is its climactic punch line.

clue.text: Damage extremely lucrative career

parts.note: to hurt is to damage

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme letters, first and last, of the next word

explanation.surface: A well-paid profession has been badly harmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun, a job, but is the verb, to rush headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to move swiftly and uncontrollably, which is to hurtle.

clue.text: Bean coming from abroad UK imports

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A legume brought into Britain from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The aduki, also spelt adzuki, is a small red bean from East Asia.

clue.text: Disease, in a manner of speaking, learner's overlooked

indicators.note: overlooked means missed out, so the learner's letter is dropped

parts.note: an inflection is a modulation of the voice, a manner of speaking
L is the learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: An illness, so to speak, that a pupil ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a hedge but is the word being trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease caused by germs entering the body is an infection.

clue.text: Female beside bar easily tempted

parts.note: a rail is a bar, as on a fence

explanation.surface: A woman at the pub counter readily gives in to temptation.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail in an old sense means morally weak, so easily led astray or tempted.

clue.text: Barbarism's not in fashion

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
the rage is the latest fashion, all the rage

explanation.surface: Savagery has gone out of style.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage is a shocking act of cruelty or wickedness, a barbarism.

clue.text: Heartless church worker suspended

indicators.note: heartless says the central letter of the word for church is removed

parts.note: an abbey is a church, as in Westminster Abbey
the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A callous church employee has been put on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes the middle B from ABBEY, leaving ABEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeyant means in abeyance, held in temporary suspension.

clue.text: Shy infidel running like the devil

indicators.note: running suggests the letters scattering, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A timid unbeliever fleeing as fast as he can.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiendishly means in the manner of a fiend, and a fiend is a devil.

clue.text: Unlikely to lash out at close quarters

definitions.meaning: stingy, mean with money, someone who will not splash out on spending

explanation.surface: A placid person who won't swing a punch even when you're right up close.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stingy, reluctant to spend, and close by in distance.
